post.caption: Edward VIII's hair parting broke coin tradition. Edward was king for only 326 days in 1936. Since Charles II, a new king's coin portrait faces the other way from the last one, and George V faced left. Edward insisted on facing left because of his hair parting. His gold sovereign was due to be struck on New Year's Day 1937, but no Edward VIII coin was ever issued in Britain. Only six gold sovereigns dated 1937 were struck as trial pieces. As Duke of Windsor, he later asked the Mint for a set, and his brother refused. In 1970, a sealed box of leftovers held 49 coins.
